messages:
maria (eng-runtime): heads up — canary for dedicated pool-7 (merge #3127) shows p95 latency doubled on short-seq text-gen workloads. Customer-reported errors + SLA alerts from two tenants.
kevin (perf): ugh. which commit in #3127 looked suspicious? any profiler output? :eyes:
maria (eng-runtime): pushing initial flamegraph + canary logs to the canary channel. TL;DR: kernel selection changed priority order -> many short requests are hitting older slow kernel path when KV cache is enabled.
sam (infra): ok bisect started. quick note: the change added kernel hint tie-breaking that prefers cache-coherent kernels, but apparently the hint logic doesn't consider sequence length.
jess (sre): we already saw SLO noise at 00:42UTC, routed alerts to oncall. impact looks limited to Dedicated customers on pool-7 with KV cache enabled. No error spikes, just latency.
tyler (cs): two enterprise customers called in. They flagged p95 regressions on their dashboards. They want an ETA.
kevin (perf): can you drop the perf-ci summary?
perf-ci-bot: perf/bench/short_seq (baseline vs PR-3127)
```
median: baseline=38ms PR=37ms (+-)
p95: baseline=84ms PR=172ms  (x2.0)
throughput: ~no change
notes: rejit path increased overhead for kvcache hits on short sequences
```
maria (eng-runtime): annotated flamegraph: majority of extra time is in `kernel_selector::choose()` and `kv_cache::apply_prefix()` due to a new policy that forces metadata validation for every request.
kevin (perf): that policy was intended for long sequences to avoid correctness regressions after the new KV checksum work. Looks like the guard is too eager.
sam (infra): bisect points to 76a2b3c (the hint/tiebreaker). Repro locally with the dedicated canary image + kvcache enabled; repeating short-seq load recreates the p95 spike.
jess (sre): staging CI smoke for dedicated passed, but perf CI flagged the regression. See perf job #4912 attached.
perf-ci-bot: job 4912 logs -> `bench_short_seq` shows 110% increase in p95. Artifact: /artifacts/perf/4912/flamegraph.svg
maria (eng-runtime): test plan: 1) hotpatch the selector to short-circuit the new metadata validation for seq_len <= 64; 2) revert commit 76a2b3c if hotpatch is risky; 3) hold dedicated rollout until stable. Thoughts?
kevin (perf): short-circuiting sounds safe and minimal. We need a microbenchmark matrix: with/without kvcache x seq_len buckets [<=32, 33-128, >128].
tyler (cs): customers want a workaround now. Can we temporarily disable KV cache for affected pools and notify customers?
sam (infra): we can toggle kvcache per-pool, but that increases token costs; also might hurt throughput. Still better than SLA hits.
jess (sre): let's hold the rollout for the remaining dedicated pools. Flagging as rollout-blocker. I'll open an incident so we have audit.
kevin (perf): I'll prepare the hotpatch PR that skips the metadata validation when `seq_len <= 64` and `kvcache.enabled == true`. Also add a metric `selector_validation_skipped` for monitoring.
maria (eng-runtime): sounds good. Do we need a full revert? If hotpatch lands quickly we can avoid revert. Revert would be noisy for other fixes in #3127.
sam (infra): agree. I'll stage the hotpatch to canary pool-7 after unit tests. If canary looks good for 30m, we can proceed to continue the rollout.
perf-ci-bot: triggered microbench matrix (short_seq buckets). queued -> job 4920.
kevin (perf): also adding a targeted test in the perf suite that simulates heavy `kvcache.apply_prefix()` churn with short sequences — to prevent regressions in CI.
tyler (cs): I'll email the two impacted customers with a short note: we identified cause, mitigation in progress, working on hotpatch, ETA ~1-2 hours.
jess (sre): incident opened: INC-2026-071. Current state: INVESTIGATING. Priority: P2. Affected: Dedicated pool-7, two customers.
maria (eng-runtime): timeline: 00:00 report -> 00:12 bisect -> 00:30 hotpatch PR open -> 00:54 canary deploy planned.
kevin (perf): if hotpatch doesn't fix it, revert is fallback. Keep rollback plan ready.
sam (infra): canary deploy of hotpatch complete. Initial p95 numbers: baseline 84ms -> post-hotpatch 88ms (within noise).
maria (eng-runtime): canary looks stable at +5% not +100%. re-run perf microbench to confirm.
perf-ci-bot: microbench 4920 results: p95 delta PR-hotpatch vs baseline = +6% (within threshold).
jess (sre): holding rollout lift: mark blocked in release board, updated incident with hotpatch success.
tyler (cs): customers updated. They appreciate the quick action.
kevin (perf): follow-ups: add unit tests for `kernel_selector` tie-breaker logic, add perf alert on `selector_validation_skipped`-> if we skip too often unexpectedly, fail early.
maria (eng-runtime): thanks everyone. Leaving this thread open until next deploy succeeds across dedicated pools. :thumbsup:
